source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Root-knot nematode disease in watermelon, which causes galls/knots on the roots (shown in a reference photo labeled "Meloidogyne: galles sur racines de melon"), is caused by Meloidogyne spp.

Control measures: practice crop rotation; plow the soil deeply, which can reduce nematode populations in the soil; destroy weeds and volunteer host plants; propagate/select rootstock varieties that are resistant to the disease when using grafted planting material; and manage soil naturally so it maintains good soil reactivity/health (soil conditions that suppress nematode buildup).
